{{Quote|It's easy to disagree with the policies of someone who has destroyed your family. Fel has a habit of being too merciful for his own good.|Aristocra Chaf'orm'bintrano|<ref name="Joiner King">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref>}}
A [[Unidentified syndic (Ina'ganet'nuruodo)|syndic]] that opposed [[Assistant Syndic]] [[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]] once belonged to a '''family''' that was among the [[Ruling Families/Legends|Ruling Families]] of the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]]. According to the account given by [[Aristocra/Legends|Aristocra]] [[Chaf'orm'bintrano]]<ref name="Joiner King" /> in [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]],<ref name="Joiner King Date">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]'' to [[35 ABY/Legends|35 ABY]].</ref> it was one of three Ruling Families that employed hives of the sentient [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] as a work force during a [[Chiss civil conflict|civil conflict]] between the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]]. As a result, the Family fell out of power<ref name="TEA" /> by [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]]<ref name="Extinction Date" /> and was destroyed by Soontir Fel<ref name="Joiner King" /> over the family's continued reliance on the Killiks.<ref name="TEA" />

{{Chiss-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The family was mentioned in ''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]'', the first installment of ''[[Star Wars: The Dark Nest Trilogy]]'', which was written by [[Troy Denning]] and published in [[2005]].<ref name="Joiner King" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' identified four of the Ruling Families that fell on the losing side of a [[Chiss civil conflict|civil conflict]] between [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Sharb/Legends|Sharb]], [[Noris/Legends|Noris]], [[Schesa/Legends|Schesa]], and [[Ornfra/Legends|Ornfra]], while two of the Ruling Families of the planets [[Catlia]] and [[Massoss/Legends|Massoss]] became [[Joiner]]s.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Since the novel clearly refers to the former, the family must have been the resident of one of the four planets.
